graph.title: Billund Airport

edges.method: slope's anti-stud clutches the side stud of the white 1x1 SNOT brick (step 27); the slope sits sideways, so it is not on the stud grid
clip on bar (red flag clip hung on the white 3L bar flagpole)

notes: Steps use the booklet's main step numbers 1-50; sub-assembly steps (19, 21, 32, 36, 37, 43, 49, 50) share the main step number.

Grid: x is 0-23 (left to right), y is 0-11 (front to back). The four 6x12 base plates sit side by side as 24x12, built right to left (p142, p143, p144, p145). The black 1x8 and 1x1 tiles form the border ring at layer 1.

Border tiles p224, p225, p227, p228, p229 and p231 (steps 2, 4, 6) are laid so that they overhang the edge of the base plate built so far; the next base plate (steps 3, 5, 7) is then slid in underneath them. The tiles therefore rest on two base plates, and that second plate is added one step later. This is how the booklet builds the base, so these tiles list the later plate in rests_on on purpose.

Nothing rests on a smooth tile: tiles only sit on top of studs. Buildings, bricks and sub-assemblies sit on studded plates, jumpers, clear plates and the cross plate. Curved roof pieces clutch only a clear plate.

The side-stud slope p240 clutches the side stud of the SNOT brick p278, so it is listed in other_joins only (rests_on is empty, position is null). p278 has one top stud, which carries tile p199 (step 37).
Most positions are estimated from isometric drawings. The roof area (steps 17-43) is approximate and some placements may be off by a stud.

Piece-to-step assignment for look-alike parts (clear 1x1/1x2 plates, white 1x1 plates, grey tiles) was inferred from the part counts in each step's legend and the totals on the parts page, so every id is used exactly once but the split between steps may be slightly off.

Step 19 builds four identical units. Step 50 builds five aeroplanes, each on the free stud of one of the five step-17 clear plates. The flag clip p256 is attached to the bar p286 and has no grid position.
